name: Shachtmanism
summary: Shachtmanism is the Marxist current built around Max Shachtman and the Workers Party that split from Trotskyism in 1940. It holds that the Soviet Union was neither capitalist nor a workers' state but a 'bureaucratic collectivist' society run by a new ruling class, and it adopts a Third Camp stance of backing neither Washington nor Moscow but the democratic struggles of workers and oppressed peoples. Its later social-democratic branch backed labor, civil rights and containment of Stalinism, while its left branch (Draper) stressed socialism from below.
scope: Classic Shachtmanism of the Workers Party and Independent Socialist League (1940-1958), built on Shachtman's writings on bureaucratic collectivism and Draper's socialism from below, with the later Social Democrats USA strand noted where it differs. It excludes Cannonite Trotskyism, state-capitalist theories (Cliff) and the neoconservatives who later drew from the milieu. Many economic and social statements were never addressed by the current and are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the social-democratic welfare programme (such as the 1966 Freedom Budget) that Shachtman's later followers backed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the labor-movement and Freedom Budget politics of the later Shachtmanites; the sources give no position on wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Shachtman wrote that capitalism and Stalinism alike block socialism and looked to democratic mass control of the economy, so market allocation is not an adherent's answer.

public-ownership.rationale: They favor collective ownership but insist that state ownership without democratic control, as in Russia, only creates a bureaucratic ruling class; the agreement is conditional.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian social-democratic politics of the later strand; tax rates are not addressed in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Shachtmanites organized in the labor movement (fighting the UAW wartime no-strike pledge) and later backed free trade unions worldwide as the core of working-class power.

property-fundamental.rationale: Their goal is collective, democratically controlled ownership of the means of production, so an inviolable right to private property contradicts their programme.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred; they wanted to replace capitalism, but the later social-democratic strand accepted tighter control as a step.

cut-welfare.rationale: Later Shachtmanites in the Socialist Party and unions pushed expanded social programmes, so welfare cuts run against their working-class politics.

worker-ownership.rationale: Draper's socialism from below puts economic decisions in workers' hands, though the sources stress democratic control of the whole economy more than firm-level ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from their insistence on democratic liberties against police-state methods; no direct statement.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; adherents of different periods would split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on civil liberty and opposition to the suppression of speech by bureaucratic rulers.

strong-leader.rationale: Shachtman treated Stalin's supreme-arbiter role and personality cult as products of bureaucratic class rule, and Draper's socialism from below rejects rule by an elite.

state-harmful.rationale: They want rule from below and oppose bureaucratic states, but they accept a democratic workers' state in transition and do not call the state unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control never featured in the sources; a labor-left current would split between civil-liberties and safety views.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from distrust of coercive state apparatuses and bureaucratic rule; domestic policing is not discussed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no settled adherent line.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the humanist socialist outlook that frames harsh rule as barbarism; criminal justice is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from a secular Marxist outlook; the sources do not address the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the classic period; inferred from commitment to equal rights and from later socialist heirs of the tradition.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from socialist support for women's liberation and civil liberties.

more-religion-public.rationale: Inferred from a secular Marxist outlook; not discussed.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Shachtman developed 'revolutionary integrationism' and his followers worked in the civil rights movement, though he preferred class-based over racial remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources say nothing on gender theory; no known position.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred from internationalist class politics; they opposed national oppression but not culture as such.

gradual-change.rationale: The early movement sought a revolutionary democratic upheaval against Stalinism and capitalism, while the later social-democratic strand favoured reform through realignment; the strands split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from working-class internationalism; migration is not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Third Camp politics distrusted both power blocs, which colours how they would see the UN; no stated position.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; they have no protectionist or free-trade programme in the sources.

nation-first.rationale: Third Camp socialism is internationalist and refuses to side with either bloc, looking instead to the world working class and colonial peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Later Shachtmanites backed some US action against Stalinism, while the classic strand opposed imperialist war; adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalist but no source states an open-borders aim; adherents divide.

limit-growth.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Marxist view that productive abundance is the base of socialism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from socialist preference for democratic state action on collective problems.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view that social structure decides outcomes, and Shachtman's warning that Stalinism could become a form of barbarism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is not discussed and the current predates the debate; no principled lean follows from its positions.

revolution-justified.rationale: Shachtman argued that Stalinist regimes can only be overturned by a revolutionary democratic upheaval of the masses.

experts-over-public.rationale: Socialism from below rejects rule by an elite or bureaucracy; the masses must run society themselves.

central-planning.rationale: Shachtman held that state-run economies without democracy produce a new exploiting class; planning is acceptable only under democratic mass control.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not discuss market socialism; adherents' economic models were not detailed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is a single-tax reform idea that this Marxist current never took up, so no lean can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian socialist outlook; not stated.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional income is not in the sources; the labor-left stress on jobs and union wages gives no clear lean.

state-directs-investment.rationale: They criticized state-run economies under a bureaucracy but favored planning under democratic control, so the answer depends on who directs.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: they aim at collective ownership rather than a spread of small holdings.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A distant Marxist aim but not emphasized by this current in any source opened.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred; socialists would put finance under public control rather than leave money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Independent unions were central to them; state-recognized bodies setting wages resemble the subordination of labor under Stalinism and fascism they opposed.

one-party-rule.rationale: Shachtman described single-party Stalinist rule as bureaucratic class rule and called for the democratic supremacy of the masses.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts democratic socialism from below; inferred from that principle.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is central: socialism is democratic control from below, and later Shachtmanites defended democracy and free unions against communism worldwide.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favor mass participation but no source states a view on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: The Trotskyist heritage and socialism from below point to workers' self-organisation, but the late social-democratic strand worked through parliaments; the strands split.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to national oppression, including Stalinist; secession is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Draper's central thesis is that rule by an elite is the 'from above' soul of socialism, which he rejects.

political-violence-never.rationale: They endorsed mass revolution against Stalinism, so violence is not rejected absolutely, though they were not militarists.

war-builds-character.rationale: Third Camp politics saw war between blocs as imperialist barbarism, not an ennobling force.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from secular Marxism and civil liberties; not discussed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from secular Marxism and the democratic principle that the masses make the laws.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: privatized coercion contradicts both collectivism and democratic public control.

military-superiority.rationale: Classic Shachtmanism rejected both blocs' arms build-up, while the later strand backed the US stance against Stalinism; adherents split by period.

ethnic-nation.rationale: They condemned national oppression and were internationalist, so an ethnically defined nation is rejected by inference.

class-struggle-history.rationale: They are Marxists whose analysis rests on class rule, and they extended it to a new bureaucratic ruling class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The socialist aim of ending class exploitation implies greater equality, though they do not frame it in terms of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims are not discussed; opposition to national oppression points one way, collectivist class politics another.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not discussed in the sources; support for colonial peoples is clear but compensation claims are not.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism, which cuts across civilization blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Draper's collective socialist ethic opposes the idea that self-interest is the moral basis of society.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They prized democratic rights and civil liberties against bureaucratic rule.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics lie outside the sources and the current's concerns.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred; Marxists generally attribute poverty and scarcity to social institutions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marxists treat industrial development as the material basis of socialism, not a disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pace of technological change is not addressed; Marxist views on productive forces are ambivalent about disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Biotechnology is outside the sources and the era of the current.

algorithmic-government.rationale: They want democratic mass control, which rules out rule by technocratic systems; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources predate the issue; civil-liberties concerns and anti-surveillance instincts balance against no stated view.

restore-past-order.rationale: Strongly progressive: their aim is socialism ahead, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Shachtman insisted on a Marxist method for analysing even new phenomena, though the later realignment strand was pragmatic.

direct-action.rationale: Early Shachtmanites stressed workplace and mass action, while the later strand focused on realignment inside the Democratic Party; the strands split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Draper's socialism from below holds that democratic ends cannot be reached by elite or bureaucratic methods.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from Marxist progressivism, which sees material development as a basis for socialism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A distant Marxist aim not emphasized by this current in the sources.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A socialist goal in the Marxist tradition, implied by their aims rather than stated in the sources.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need rather than profit is core to the Marxist programme they hold.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist theory of capitalist exploitation is their baseline, and they also held that Stalinism had its own class exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They rejected the one-party dictatorship that Leninism became and equated socialism with democracy; the term is disowned by the democratic strand.

collective-farming.rationale: Stalinist collectivization was treated as bureaucratic class rule and coercion rather than socialism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: They called both camps imperialist and stressed Stalinist imperialism, so capitalism is not treated as the sole cause.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: contradicts the socialist view of collective provision.

harm-principle.rationale: The sources do not discuss liberal liberty doctrines; socialists accept restrictions beyond harm to others in some cases.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed directly; they stressed class and national rights.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imperialist wars; not stated.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic voice is central to their politics, and they saw mass democratic upheaval as the check on rulers.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: customer-and-exit governance contradicts democratic socialist control.

positive-liberty.rationale: Shachtman speaks of 'socialist freedom', and socialist freedom requires material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; Marxists treat economic power as primary.

hereditarian-race.rationale: They opposed racial hierarchy and developed revolutionary integrationism.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation contradicts democratic worker representation and independent unions.

total-state.rationale: Shachtman condemned the totalitarian bureaucratic state as a new class rule.

national-rebirth.rationale: Inferred: fascist-style rebirth slogans were the kind of barbarism they opposed.

territorial-expansion.rationale: They condemned Stalinist imperialist expansion and national oppression.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal elite rule is a form of socialism-from-above-type hierarchy they reject.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labor contradicts the principle of workers' self-emancipation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is not discussed; Marxism has both ideology-critique and scientific claims, so no lean is clear.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not discuss moral philosophy; Shachtman's humanist appeals to freedom are consistent with either answer.

single-common-good.rationale: Inferred: Marxists see society as divided by class interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Inferred; the sources opened do not state their position on Israel, though the tradition is understood to have accepted it after the Holocaust.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not discussed in the sources opened.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival politics are not discussed, and nothing in the sources gives a lean.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Socialism from below places decisions in the hands of workers and the public.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from their preference for public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from the interventionist left outlook.

economic-freedom.rationale: They hold that political freedom requires socialist democracy, not market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Contradicts their materialist and democratic approach; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: They opposed national oppression, including Stalin's, and sided with colonial peoples.

force-without-un.rationale: Adherents split: classic Shachtmanism rejected imperialist war while later followers backed US action against Stalinism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular Marxist outlook implies a rationalist lean, but the sources do not discuss faith versus reason.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work requirements were not discussed; inferred disagreement from the labor-left defence of unconditional social provision.

class-collaboration.rationale: They reject class collaboration, though the late strand allied with unions and liberals.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from humanism and opposition to cultural destruction under bureaucratic rule.

dominated-front.rationale: The Third Camp refuses to tie itself to any power bloc, so a front of dominated countries led by states would not be favored.

workers-nation.rationale: Their internationalist class outlook opposes organizing along national lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the socialist equality principle.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest bans are not discussed and conflict with the Marxist focus on ownership of production rather than lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: They fought segregation and advocated revolutionary integrationism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The ruling-class analysis of the bureaucratic state is central, though they held that democratic states can be won.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed; the current predates the climate debate.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theory contrary to their class analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic principle.

national-mission.rationale: Third Camp rejects any state's mission to impose its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist theory is not discussed in the sources; later socialist heirs accept it, so a weak inferred agree.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not directly stated, but they described the Stalinist bureaucracy as a privileged ruling class; for Western politicians no line is given.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics contradicts their humanist egalitarian outlook.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from their democratic politics and condemnation of Stalinist police abuses; not stated in the sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A minimal state contradicts their goal of democratic collective ownership of the economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: It contradicts the integrationism Shachtman developed in the civil rights movement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Core egalitarian humanist premise of socialism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Shachtman called the Stalinist order nationally limited and not socialist; socialism needs international revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not discuss settler colonialism; adherents' views on Israel and similar cases would vary.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law politics are not in the sources; the secular outlook and the autonomy of minorities conflict.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restrictions on conversion contradict the civil liberties they defended against Stalinist regimes.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious ban on slaughter conflicts with the secular outlook of the current; inferred, not discussed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from a secular Marxist outlook; school religion is not discussed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: They rejected the claim that a bureaucratic state defends socialism, and held socialism means democratic mass rule.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic legitimacy is central: rulers must rest on the masses.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims conflict with their internationalism; not discussed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They endorse revolution against Stalinism, so absolute pacifism is not theirs.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Contradicts Marxist class cooperation and socialism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred civil-libertarian; later anti-communists may differ.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resonates with socialism from below; not stated in those terms.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not discussed; democratic mass control is stressed more than checks between bodies.

vanguard-party.rationale: The strand moved from Leninist vanguardism toward democratic self-emancipation, though early Shachtmanites were Leninists.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Their politics centered on the working class, and later the Freedom Budget aimed at ending poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not discussed, and a labor-left current could favor either.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Workers Party fought the wartime no-strike pledge in the UAW.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist view puts poverty in social institutions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: It contradicts the integrationism they developed in the civil rights movement.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed; their democracy is about mass participation and election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Contradicts their democratic stance; Stalinist emergency rule was their target.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not discussed in the sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: They condemned Stalinist state control of information and the disenfranchisement of workers.

party-commands-army.rationale: Stalinist party rule over the army is part of the bureaucratic structure they condemned.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship law is not discussed; internationalism suggests mild opposition but no source says so.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from socialism from below and the egalitarian tradition; not stated.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Leninist heritage versus democratic outlook; adherents split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational union is not discussed; it did not exist in their classic period.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential command powers contradict the democratic control from below they held.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the current's concerns.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by clergy contradicts both secularism and democratic rule by the masses.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Third Camp refused to back either belligerent camp, though that is abstention rather than working for defeat, and the later strand abandoned it in the Cold War.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Contradicts liberty they defended against bureaucratic censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; they criticized personalized rule, so a mild lean against.

recall-officials.rationale: Democratic control from below implies the removal of officials by those who chose them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Split: Third Camp neutrality versus later support for the US role.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed; collectivist politics do not favor universal homeownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The sources do not discuss militias; Marxist tradition has the idea but this current did not emphasize it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural romanticism contradicts the Marxist progressive view of industrial development.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Division of nations is not discussed in the sources opened, though Germany's partition would raise the case.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectualism is not in the sources; Shachtmanites were themselves largely intellectuals.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed; the current's universalism is consistent with both answers.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from a humanist socialist outlook that rejects state killing; not discussed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from socialist support for secular schooling and equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from a secular scientific Marxist outlook; not discussed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; the civil-liberties instinct and the socialist moral concern pull opposite ways.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not discussed; internationalism suggests a preference for residence-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from their opposition to national oppression, though language policy is not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; secular egalitarian instincts and civil liberty pull opposite ways.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not discussed; no lean can be inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed; the current predates the debt-relief debate.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Third Camp stance: colonial peoples need social as well as political liberation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from democratic supremacy of the masses.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: They rejected the Stalinist road of restricting freedom for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not discussed; internationalism supports solidarity but Shachtmanites did not state a view on state aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not discussed; they were skeptical of arms build-ups but the sources do not address national deterrents.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; no lean can be drawn.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not discussed; the socialist preference for democratic control of finance gives a weak inferred disagree.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not discussed; Shachtmanites backed negotiated settlements in Vietnam, suggesting a weak disagree.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from their collectivist view of property; not stated in the sources.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Shachtmanism's defining thesis is that the USSR is bureaucratic collectivist, explicitly neither capitalist nor a workers' state; it is also not socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not discussed; the current predates environmental risk policy.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents split: Third Camp neutrality versus the later strand's support for Western alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from opposition to Stalinist annexations.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; secularism favors curbing clerical power but civil liberties temper it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not discussed; ceremonial heads of state are irrelevant to their programme.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed; opposition to national oppression suggests mild disagreement.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed; Shachtman's views on Hong Kong-style arrangements are not in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Stalin's cult was condemned as a product of bureaucratic rule.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax contradicts egalitarian aims; inferred rather than stated.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist materialism holds that circumstances shape people, though the sources do not discuss the question directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule above law contradicts democratic control; inferred from their criticism of unaccountable rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not discussed in the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed regimes are not discussed and contradict democratic rule by the masses.

leader-cult.rationale: Shachtman explicitly treated the Stalin personality cult as a product of the bureaucracy's structure and condemned the regime.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Contradicts their view that Russia was not socialist; this is a Stalinist-era formula.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is not discussed; Marxists favor it in peasant contexts but the sources do not say.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not discussed in the sources opened.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contradicts their opposition to national oppression.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy contradicts the civil liberties they defended against regimes of all kinds.

women-must-cover.rationale: Legal dress mandates contradict civil liberties and secular egalitarian politics.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic unity is not discussed; internationalist class politics cut against ethnic blocs.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed in the sources opened; the Marxist debate on the topic is older than their positions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not discussed; the current's internationalism leans to struggle where people live, but nothing states it.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: they were not pacifists and endorsed revolutionary force, though they opposed imperialist armies; abolition is not discussed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Draper's socialism from below opposes rule by an inherited elite; inferred from that principle.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed in any source opened; no known adherent line.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the mainstream socialist stance on the family; marriage law is not discussed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: they distrusted coercive state organs under bureaucratic rule but never advocated abolishing policing.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist theme and plausible for them, but the sources opened do not discuss alienation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animals are not discussed by this current; no known position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal welfare is not in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from their Third Camp opposition to fascist and Stalinist barbarism alike; constitutional design is not discussed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Shachtman looked to mass democratic upheaval, not a small armed group, so this is inferred as a rejection.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Classic Third Camp rejected imperialist covert wars, though Bay of Pigs reactions show late-strand ambiguity; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is outside the sources.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not discussed; socialists would rather replace than break up concentrated capital.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from labor-movement protection of employees.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contradicts their anti-racism and working-class unity.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not discussed; adherents had no distinctive line.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Shachtman wrote that world capitalism is doomed along with Stalinism, so he doubted its lasting adaptation, though he did not predict automatic collapse.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxist method treats capitalism as having created the material basis for socialism, and Shachtman applied Marx's historical framework flexibly.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The later social-democratic strand backed state programmes like the Freedom Budget and the earlier strand collective class action.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; participatory democracy fits but sortition is not stated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: They sided with colonial peoples against imperialism and nationalist movements, as noted in sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty law is not discussed in the sources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: They opposed imperialism and aligned with colonial nationalist forces such as the Indian National Congress.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture critique is not in the sources opened.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They aimed at democratic control of the whole economy, not at small communes.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from socialist critique of capitalist power; not stated.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; they prized both democracy and civil liberties.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not discussed; materialism favors social change over cultural renewal.

decide-locally.rationale: Mass democracy implies local participation but no source states a position on decentralization.

defeat-communism.rationale: Shachtman argued Stalinist regimes must be overthrown by a mass democratic upheaval, and later Shachtmanites backed containment of communism and democracy movements; the means differ from conservatives.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from secularism and opposition to religious rule.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and Third Camp refusal to submit to blocs.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not discussed; they looked to world working-class action.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; late anti-communists backed democracy promotion while the classic strand saw imperialist wars everywhere.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic legal doctrine not discussed by the current.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secular and democratic: authority rests on the masses.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not discussed and postdates the current.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from democratic principle and condemnation of personalized rule.

elective-rulers.rationale: Democratic rule resting on the masses is central.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: They favored racial equality but sought class-based remedies; late Shachtmanites (Rustin tradition) were ambivalent, so inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from the defence of civil liberties; constitutional entrenchment is not discussed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from internationalism that bans on foreigners are disfavored; not discussed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: They condemned imperial influence and Stalinist domination of neighboring countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: They fought racial discrimination and segregation.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from civil-rights and socialist commitments.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not discussed in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is outside the current's concerns.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from opposition to nationalist chauvinism.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from internationalist outlook that a nation-centred history curriculum is disfavored.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial contradicts their anti-fascist stance and they compared Stalinism to Nazi barbarism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Anti-exploitation Marxist analysis implies that returns should go to labor, not ownership alone.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from equal citizenship principle.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from social-democratic support for collective provision.

industrial-unions.rationale: Their UAW activity belonged to the industrial union movement of the CIO era.

informal-organisation.rationale: They organized parties and tendencies and labor-movement work, not informal groups.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They held that democratic freedom is a universal aim.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit schemes are not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Restrictions on marriage by religion contradict the civil liberties they defended.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; they stressed class while opposing racial segregation.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: They condemned Stalinist suppression of national resistance and revolts like East Berlin 1953.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts their anti-racist universalism, though the sources do not discuss Islam.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the full-employment stress of the Freedom Budget they backed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed; they organized industrial workers as the agent of socialism.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure rules are not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: They held a class framework distinct from both capitalism and Stalinism.

local-production.rationale: Localism is not in the sources.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural critique is not in the sources opened.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist method, though Shachtman rejected a rigid mechanical sequence of social orders.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Army political roles contradict democratic rule by the masses; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from democratic majority principle.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred preference for public provision, though providers are not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed; the Cuban-style idea does not fit their democratic emphasis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born contradicts working-class internationalism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third Camp stance: they reject both capitalism and Stalinist 'communism' in favor of democratic socialism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: They endorsed revolutionary struggle and were not pacifists.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Socialism from below rejects paternalist elite duty in favor of self-emancipation.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from secular and liberal social outlook.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Gender theory is not in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Third Camp suggests yes, later strand supported US alliances; split.

non-intervention.rationale: They condemned Stalinist and imperialist intervention but also supported solidarity for democracy movements such as Solidarity.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: bureaucratic selection recalls the ruling bureaucracy they criticized.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the internet postdates the current.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on democratic control from below; not stated.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; not discussed in the sources.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labor politics are not discussed in the sources.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not discussed; they accepted parliaments in the late period, soviets earlier.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Draper's socialism from below means ordinary people making decisions themselves.

party-own-road.rationale: Shachtman rejected Moscow's direction of other countries' parties and held that Stalinism is a national bureaucratic system.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from internationalism that national pride teaching is rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialism means collective ownership of productive means, not personal items.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: A materialist Marxist outlook contradicts framing politics as a spiritual struggle.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are not discussed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from Marxist critique of capitalist control of institutions.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of arbitrary bureaucratic rule.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not discussed; internationalism disfavors nationalist pronatalism.

property-franchise.rationale: A property qualification contradicts the democratic principle of mass rule.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from democratic control from below; not stated.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from public control of the economy; money creation is not discussed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy laws contradict the secular civil liberties they defended.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial limits on the franchise contradict the integrationist position stated by Shachtman and the sources' record of civil-rights work.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from socialism from below; not stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from anti-Nazi and anti-Stalinist condemnation of national oppression.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from class solidarity across regions.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the sources do not discuss.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Theology is outside the current's concerns.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from Marxist materialism; not discussed.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed; secular instincts and civil liberty pull opposite ways.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining a nation by religion contradicts their internationalism.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from labor-left politics; not discussed.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They urged mass resistance to bureaucratic rulers.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Contradicts their opposition to national oppression.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from egalitarianism that unequal development stages are disfavored; not discussed.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Marxist theme implied but not stated in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious reform is outside the current's concerns.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from socialist equality principles; not discussed.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from opposition to national oppression.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Contradicts their historical materialism and civil-rights politics.

socialized-care.rationale: Domestic labor is not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Later social-democratic strand might agree, classic strand sought socialism; split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Contradicts civil liberties they defended against Stalinist rule.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Third Camp slogan was 'neither Washington nor Moscow', but the later strand sided with the West; the strands split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Shachtman condemned the Stalinist suppression of opposition.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Shachtman compared the Stalinist empire to Nazi rule and held capitalism and Stalinism as obstacles, though they did not treat the left alike.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Contradicts their internationalism and materialist view of history.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Calling for rulers' removal by religious law contradicts their secular democratic politics.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-democratic view that economic power produces political power; the 1953 text ties state property to power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: They were committed activists and organizers, which contradicts withdrawal.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Socialist assumption; not stated in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is outside the current's concerns.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not discussed; the current focused on class rule rather than dependency theory.

independent-unions.rationale: Free trade unions are central to the strand that backed unions and Solidarity against Stalinist states, while Shachtman held that the Stalinist bureaucracy depends on disenfranchising workers.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: This is the heart of Shachtman's denial that Russia is socialist and of Draper's socialism from below.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the democratic-socialist commitment to public ownership under democratic control; local services are not specifically discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: Socialism from below favours direct democratic control, and a further check on elected bodies is inferred to be unwelcome.

municipal-property.rationale: The current wanted collective ownership under democratic control of the whole society, not municipal ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Socialism from below stresses democratic control from the base, but the sources do not take a stand on confederal binding power.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its labor-movement politics of living wages; no stated doctrine.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for the 1940-1958 current.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the stress on democratic freedoms against bureaucratic control; the topic is anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Shachtman's critique of bureaucratic collectivism condemns a ruling bureaucracy that uses people as means, and demands socialist freedom and democratic control.

spiritual-nature.rationale: A secular Marxist current that never addressed this; no clear stated position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The current backed civil rights through labor and class politics rather than separate racial organising; its later strand worked within the integrationist civil rights movement.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Third Camp backed neither bloc, but Shachtman later backed containment of Stalinism and a negotiated approach in Vietnam, so adherents were split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: Marxist internationalism treats class as the basis of politics rather than language, and the sources discuss no nation-building by language; Shachtman did back national self-determination of oppressed peoples.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the current's commitment to secular, democratic working-class politics rules out communal electorates; the sources do not mention them.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the Third Camp opposed both Washington and Moscow imperialism and it treated nationalist conspiracy claims as a cover for state power; the sources do not discuss partition plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic welfare and labour programme that later Shachtmanites backed; sources do not discuss tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the classic current predates environmental taxation and Marxists were split over market tools.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and a classic Marxist current of the 1940s-50s had no stated position on this duty.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from Marxist class analysis, which does not ground politics in distinct women's values; the sources never address the question.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp's opposition to both blocs' arms race; the sources do not discuss disarmament by agreement, and the later strand backed containment.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from socialism from below and democratic control; Draper and Shachtman condemned the secret diplomacy of Stalin, such as the pact with Hitler, but the sources do not state a rule.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the current was concerned with workers' control and political democracy, not with capital flows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed; Shachtmanites distrusted state power, including the bureaucratic collectivist state, yet backed defence of democratic states, so no clear line.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Third Camp opposed both blocs' wars but the Workers Party did not endorse general refusal of orders; later Shachtmanites backed containment, so adherents split.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Shachtmanism centred on the labour movement and independent unions, with later followers deeply tied to AFL-CIO unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as a reform the social-democratic branch might accept while the left branch saw it as palliative.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the socialist and social-democratic commitment to public spending, such as the Freedom Budget; not directly stated.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp backing of oppressed peoples and anti-colonial struggles; the sources do not discuss global economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Marxist tradition and socialism from below stress workers building new democratic organs, but the social-democratic branch accepted existing democratic states; adherents split, leaning left.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Shachtmanism held to a collectivist, democratically planned economy as the socialist goal, so no-blueprint pluralism is inferred as rejected.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed in a mid-century Marxist current; inferred from the Marxist view that capital is a social relation to be abolished, not extended to nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: As internationalist Marxists the Shachtmanites rejected nationalism and its mystique, putting class and democratic struggle first.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the social-democratic welfare politics of later Shachtmanites.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; the Third Camp backed oppressed peoples and civil rights, but the sources show no internal-colonial theory.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marxist materialism treats human nature as historically shaped, yet Shachtman and Draper appealed to democratic human values; the sources do not settle it.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and civil-liberties stress of the current, which opposed both state and commercial control of opinion; not directly stated.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the current's secular Marxism, which treats religion as ideology and not as a source of truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from socialism-from-below support for working farmers; the current wrote little on agriculture.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Third Camp opposition to both Washington and Moscow cuts against arms, while the Social Democrats USA branch backed containment, so the strands split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Shachtmanism held that workers must organize independently of both capitalist parties and the Stalinist bureaucracy, as the Workers Party did.

ban-fgm.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the current's support for the rights of oppressed peoples and women.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the current's civil-rights and equality commitments; the issue itself is not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the socialist preference for collective and democratic control over reliance on private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the current's democratic socialism from below, which rejects hereditary or unelected authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the current had no environmental doctrine and the statement pits two commitments against each other.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the current's support for civil liberties and opposition to harsh punishment of workers and the poor.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the current stressed internationalism but had no language policy.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the Workers Party's and later followers' support for strong, solidaristic labour unions over open-shop rules.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the later Social Democrats USA backing for civil-rights and voting-access measures.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the current's secular Marxist, democratic-rights outlook, which opposes state privilege for any religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from socialism from below: democracy is more than electing rulers and requires mass control from below, though free elections are essential.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a mid-century left milieu that supported personal freedoms and opposed moralistic state control.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the current's core insistence on democratic liberties and its condemnation of totalitarian control of information.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the social-democratic welfare programme (such as the 1966 Freedom Budget) of Shachtman's later followers, which favoured guaranteed social programs.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights for women follow from the socialist-democratic principles of the current and are uncontested among its adherents.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not discussed; Marxists in this milieu traced women's oppression chiefly to class society, with religion a secondary factor.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the current's anti-racism, such as support for the civil-rights movement; not stated in the sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the later social-democratic strand's support for state action on equality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; first-claim property theory has no place in the current's writings.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the later social-democratic strand's anti-totalitarian internationalism; the sources do not discuss international criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: a secular Marxist current would reject scriptural literalism, though the sources never discuss religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp backing of oppressed peoples' democratic struggles and socialism's equality aims; sources do not discuss this directly.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Shachtman broke with Trotsky in 1940 precisely by refusing unconditional defence of the USSR, calling it a bureaucratic collectivist exploiting class state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the stress on democracy and socialism from below; though council systems appeal, Draper favours direct democratic control by the people.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from secular socialism's opposition to privileged religious establishments; sources do not discuss national churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp support for oppressed peoples' self-determination; sources do not discuss territorial autonomy directly.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp's democratic self-determination principle; sources do not discuss plebiscites directly.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred as split: self-determination favours redrawing, while internationalism favours stable borders; sources are silent.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: a labour movement current aims at material abundance for workers, not austerity; sources do not discuss simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, anti-imperialist stance, which would oppose barring citizens from settling anywhere; sources are silent.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the current's commitment to equality of the sexes in socialist politics; sources do not discuss conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Socialism from below and Third Camp internationalism put democratic class struggle ahead of ancestral-land duty; inferred, not discussed.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Shachtman condemned bureaucratic collectivism for police terror and denial of democratic rights, so killing without trial is firmly rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Shachtman backed neither Washington nor Moscow, and Stalinist regimes were seen as bureaucratic collectivist, so close ties with China are inferred to be disfavoured.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Third Camp stresses workers' internationalism over national kin; the sources do not discuss minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Socialism holds productive resources in common under democratic control; compensation to all is inferred from that, not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Marxists critique the idea of labour as property while valuing democratic freedom; the sources do not address self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Later Shachtmanites backed a labor-oriented social-democratic programme; cutting regressive consumption taxes is inferred from it.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Freedom Budget politics of later Shachtmanites favoured broad social programmes, so a universal rather than targeted approach is inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Draper's socialism from below makes democratic control by the people central, and the party-state apparatus a ruling-class barrier, so intermediaries between people and leader are rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Opposition to a ruling class and for democratic control implies opposition to special privileges, inferred rather than stated.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Socialism from below is a secular, class-based politics; the sources do not discuss denominations.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Socialism from below looks forward to a freer technological society; a return to ancestral values is inferred to be rejected.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Support for civil rights and democratic freedoms implies backing for women's equal divorce rights; the sources do not discuss it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Democratic socialists favoured public ownership but Third Camp internationalism makes national control less central; adherents' view is inferred only.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the socialist critique of capitalist property relations, which treats the resulting inequality as unjust.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the social-democratic strand of the current that backed labor and redistributive reform.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Shachtman and his followers made the civil rights struggle central to their labor-centred politics, which implies racism remained a main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Third Camp backing of the democratic struggles of the oppressed, including civil rights direct action.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Marxist view that socialism frees people from toil, with no sourced position on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the Third Camp aim of workers' democratic internationalism rather than balancing rival power centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the classical Marxist framework the current worked within.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from the Third Camp internationalism, which put workers' solidarity across borders above national loyalty.

material-over-identity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the current's support for civil rights and the oppressed alongside labor, rather than ranking one above the other.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Shachtman held that a ruling party controlling the economy produced bureaucratic collectivism, a new class society, and rejected socialism without workers' democratic control.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should be independent of the state and of any ruling party.
missingStatements.rationale: Free trade unions are central to the strand that backed unions and Solidarity against Stalinist states, while Shachtman held that the Stalinist bureaucracy depends on disenfranchising workers.

missingStatements.text: A society cannot be called socialist unless the working class itself holds real political power.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the heart of Shachtman's denial that Russia is socialist and of Draper's socialism from below.

notes: Strands differ: left Shachtmanism (Draper, New Politics) holds the Third Camp line and opposed realignment; the social-democratic strand (Shachtman after 1958, Social Democrats USA) backed the Democratic Party, labor and a negotiated Vietnam peace, and moved more anti-communist. Israel and many cultural questions are not covered by the sources opened and are low-confidence.
